name: Argus Apparel Clothing Manufacturers
old_description: Custom Clothing Manufacturers You Can Trust for Quality, Style & Speed
about:
Argus Apparel operates from Los Angeles, California, where all production is carried out in-house. The company does not disclose a founding year or ownership structure, and no founders are named in its public materials. It presents itself as a U.S.-based custom clothing manufacturer serving brands of all sizes.

The shop handles the full apparel development cycle: design and concept translation, material sourcing from domestic and international suppliers, and cut-and-sew manufacturing for sportswear, T-shirts, private-label lines, swimwear, sweatshirts, and hoodies. Decoration capabilities include custom embroidery, screen printing, and sublimation printing. The company advertises both small-batch and bulk production runs with fast turnaround and consistent color accuracy, though it does not publish facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures.

Clients range from first-time designers and startups to established activewear brands and sports teams. Argus cites work with "small team orders" through to "large-scale launches" and emphasizes support for niche requests and low minimum-order quantities. Industries served include fashion, activewear, sportswear, and private-label apparel.

The company positions its differentiation on domestic production, ethical manufacturing practices, eco-conscious material options, and a partnership model that includes design guidance and transparent pricing with no hidden fees. It promotes a "personal touch" and aims to simplify the path from concept to delivery for brands that want control and speed.

name: Arieca Inc.
old_description: A new era of thermal interface materials for semiconductor cooling.
about:
Arieca Inc. operates from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, where it develops advanced thermal interface materials for semiconductor cooling. The company’s patented Liquid Metal Embedded Elastomer (LMEE) technology is designed to deliver both high thermal conductivity and mechanical reliability across diverse semiconductor applications.

Beyond material supply, Arieca provides engineering services that span assembly process development, thermal performance testing, reliability testing, and transition to high-volume production partners. The team works directly with customers to create system-level thermal solutions that are manufacturable at scale, rather than offering standalone materials.

The company targets the automotive, high-performance computing, and AI-enabled consumer electronics markets. A noted collaboration with ROHM produced a reference design for efficient silicon carbide MOSFET cooling, demonstrating engagement with power electronics manufacturers. Arieca also participates in industry forums such as IMAPS ThermCon, PCIM, and SEMI-THERM.

Arieca positions its LMEE platform as a differentiator that combines superior thermal performance with exceptional mechanical reliability, aiming to solve thermal management challenges at the system level rather than through material alone.

name: Arizona Custom Solar
about:
Arizona Custom Solar operates from Scottsdale, Arizona. The founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed on the company's website. The business presents itself as a local solar installation provider serving Arizona homeowners.

The company installs residential photovoltaic systems using black-on-black panels described as sleek and modern. It partners with Tesla to integrate Powerwall battery storage for backup power during outages. Services include 24/7 energy monitoring, system design, permitting, installation, and a detach-and-reinstall service for roof repairs. The website references "Best-in-Class Equipment Installed on Over 100,000 Homes," though this figure may reflect industry-wide deployments rather than the company's own volume. Online reviews cite 92 Google ratings with a 97.7% five-star claim.

The primary customer base appears to be Arizona homeowners seeking rooftop solar and battery backup. Reviews mention projects ranging from standard installations to complex detach-and-reinstall jobs coordinated with roofing contractors such as United Contracting Group. No commercial or industrial clients are explicitly referenced.

Arizona Custom Solar emphasizes a "Guaranteed Lowest Price," a 25-year warranty, and round-the-clock monitoring as differentiators. The Tesla partnership is highlighted as a way to give customers control over energy during grid outages. Crews are repeatedly described in reviews as professional, respectful, and thorough.

name: Arizona Electrical Apparatus
old_description: Arizona Electrical Apparatus, Inc. was founded in 1996 as a circuit breaker repair shop.
about:
Arizona Electrical Apparatus, Inc. was founded in 1996 in Tucson, Arizona, as a circuit breaker repair shop. The company is privately owned by Sal Gonzalez, who serves as president and owner, and has grown from a small repair operation into a multi-facility service and equipment provider.

Today AEA provides maintenance, testing, installation, and commissioning services for power distribution and motor control systems, and supplies apparatus such as switchgear, circuit breakers, transformers, relays, drives, and motor starters. It operates as an OEM and authorized distributor for major brands including ABB, GE, Eaton, Siemens, and Square D, and manufactures custom switchgear in-house. As of 2018 the company employed 55 people across three buildings totaling over 80,000 square feet of shop and warehouse space, with 25,000 square feet of warehouse inventory and five acres of outdoor transformer and switchgear storage.

AEA serves mining, utility, oil and gas, government and military, municipal, and ski resort customers. Its utility work includes staff augmentation and turn-key project execution for power generation facilities, while government contracts involve switchgear supply and onsite circuit breaker retrofits. The company also supports oil and gas operations with custom solutions to reduce downtime.

The company emphasizes a safety-first culture, ongoing employee safety training, and core values of teamwork, diversity, excellence, reliability, and customer service. Its stated mission is to safely and profitably provide mining and power distribution companies, large industries, and municipalities with quality power distribution and motor control products and services while maintaining a safe, efficient, and professional workplace.

name: Arizona Fashion Source
old_description: Adea Everyday Luxury makes layering tops, bodysuits and camisoles that are inspired by the Italian passion for exquisite fabric, expert tailoring and impeccable fit.
about:
Adea Everyday Luxury operates from Tempe, Arizona, but its origins trace to 2002 just outside Florence, Italy. The brand was founded as a women-owned, women-led venture with European sensibilities and American roots, inspired by the Italian passion for exquisite fabric and intentional living.

The company manufactures layering tops, bodysuits, and camisoles in the United States using premium Italian fabrics. Production runs are kept to small batches to minimize waste, and the brand emphasizes sustainability throughout its process. Adea holds Certified Carbon Neutral status and supports FABRIC, a non-profit fashion incubator and manufacturer that aims to disrupt the industry sustainably.

Adea serves the women's apparel market directly through its e-commerce channels, offering collections that include plus-size, active, and travel lines. The brand has showcased at Phoenix Fashion Week and collaborates with organizations like USA for UNHCR on limited-edition, made-to-order pieces that deliver in two to three weeks.

The business was started to bring the essence of Italian living — slow, simple, intentional — into everyday layering. Founders cite a belief that well-made products using exquisite fabrics deliver lasting value and reduce waste through longevity and versatility.

name: Arizona Solar Wave
old_description: Don’t Be A Slave To The Meter. Get Control With Arizona Solar Wave.
about:
Arizona Solar Wave operates from Mesa, Arizona, where it has provided solar energy solutions for more than 25 years. The company was established to address the state's growing energy challenges and is structured around a team of consultants, financing specialists, and installers who manage projects from assessment to commissioning.

The firm designs and installs photovoltaic systems for both residential and commercial properties, integrating battery storage and electric-vehicle charging infrastructure where required. A proprietary online tool, called Solar Wizard, helps customers estimate system size, potential savings, and environmental impact before a site visit. The company does not manufacture equipment; instead it sources panels, inverters, and batteries from third-party suppliers and coordinates permitting, installation, and utility interconnection.

Customers include homeowners seeking to reduce utility bills, businesses aiming to offset operational energy costs, and electric-vehicle owners who need charging capacity. The company's marketing materials reference primary residences, commercial facilities, and EV owners as typical client segments.

Arizona Solar Wave emphasizes a simplified purchasing model that aims to deploy the least capital for the highest return, a philosophy it describes as underpromising and overdelivering. The company cites its long-term project success and integrated in-house team as key differentiators in a market often fragmented between sales, finance, and installation contractors.

about:
Arizona Uniform & Apparel operates from Tucson, Arizona, where it was founded more than three decades ago by Alex Cantu and Laurie Ryberg, who remain CEO and co‑owner/vice president respectively. The business began as a direct‑sale alternative to traditional uniform rental and laundry services, aiming to give organizations ownership of their apparel without long‑term contracts.

The company provides end‑to‑end managed uniform programs and promotional‑product campaigns. Its services span custom program development, inventory warehousing and just‑in‑time fulfillment, branded online ordering portals with budget controls and approval workflows, and promotional‑product sourcing, kitting, and distribution. A staff of roughly 50 supports clients ranging from 50‑person teams to multi‑site workforces of 5,000.

Clients include businesses expanding their footprint, organizations frustrated by fragmented ordering, and brands needing consistent identity across departments or locations. A noted example is Pest Friends Orange County, a pest‑control company that sourced uniforms through Arizona Uniform. The firm also serves HR, operations, and procurement teams looking to centralize purchasing and reduce administrative load.

Arizona Uniform positions its direct‑sale model as the core differentiator: no rental agreements, no laundry fees, and transparent pricing. It emphasizes ongoing account management, regular program reviews, and the ability to adapt programs as customer needs evolve.

about:
Ark Plastics LLC runs a custom injection molding operation from Beaver Dam, Wisconsin. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or ownership structure.

The shop houses molding machines with clamping forces ranging from 120 to 500 tons and shot capacities from 6 to 60 ounces within a 20,000-square-foot building equipped with truck and ground-level loading docks. Beyond molding, the company provides short- and long-run production, product sampling, secondary operations such as drilling and tapping, assembly, and packaging. Support services include design assistance, master unit die (MUD) programs, and custom inventory and delivery programs.

Ark Plastics primarily serves manufacturers of consumer products, offering high-quality plastic components at competitive prices. Its customer base includes businesses seeking both prototype and production quantities, though specific industry sectors beyond consumer goods are not detailed in its public information.

The company emphasizes its ability to tailor inventory and delivery schedules, provide design support, and leverage master unit die tooling to reduce lead times and tooling costs. It also promotes aggressive pricing as a core differentiator.

name: Arkansas Diesel Engines
old_description: We pay TOP MARKET PRICES and always pay quickly, so you can keep your cash flow working for you.
about:
Arkansas Diesel Engines operates from Little Rock, Arkansas, where it has served the diesel engine market for over two decades. The company was established as a remanufacturing supply business focused on diesel engine cores and components, though the exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company specializes in the wholesale and export of used diesel engines, complete engines, and a broad range of engine components including heads, blocks, crankshafts, connecting rods, injectors, fuel pumps, turbochargers, water pumps, oil pumps, air compressors, electronic control modules, starters, alternators, and EGR system parts. It maintains a core buying program with a published list of sought‑after part numbers for brands such as Caterpillar, Cummins, and Detroit Diesel, and offers parts sourcing for items not in stock.

Arkansas Diesel Engines supplies truck parts dealers, engine rebuilders, and the broader rebuilding and truck parts industries across the United States and internationally. Its product lineup covers engines and components for Cummins, Detroit Diesel, Caterpillar, International, Mack, Mercedes‑Benz, Ford, GM, Volvo, and John Deere applications, serving heavy‑duty trucking, construction, agricultural, and industrial equipment sectors.

The company states that its goal is to provide the highest level of products available, emphasizing that its success is tied to customer success. It pledges professionalism, integrity, loyalty, and honesty in customer relationships, and highlights its technical knowledge as a differentiator in the global diesel core market.

name: Arkansas Industrial Computing / AIC Rail
old_description: Solutions for maintenance, manufacturing, and repair of rolling stock world wide
about:
Arkansas Industrial Computing (AIC) was established in 1993 in North Little Rock, Arkansas, as a systems integrator for manufacturing and machine control, providing machine automation and data collection services to manufacturers. In 1996, the company began offering products and services to the rail industry under the AIC Rail brand.

The company develops software suites for rail maintenance and manufacturing, including the Railcar Integrated Maintenance Suite (RIMS) for component tracking, association, and registration, and the Shop Management Suite (SMS) for production and quality control in wheel, railcar, and locomotive shops. AIC also supplies equipment for wheelset manufacturing and quality assurance, such as ultrasonic and magnetic particle testing systems, all integrated with its software for data collection and compliance. The company reports serving customers in eight countries and most U.S. states and Canadian provinces, with over 95% of railcar wheels mounted in North America documented using its products.

AIC Rail serves freight, transit, and locomotive repair shops, new car builders, and general manufacturing operations. Its solutions are used by wheel and motor shops to enforce quality inspections, track components, and manage production data in real time. The company partners with other technology providers to deliver complete rail solutions while maintaining priority support for those products.

The business was founded to provide machine automation and data collection services, and its differentiation lies in the seamless integration of equipment with software applications, real-time production visibility, and enforcement of quality and supervisory functions across manufacturing environments.
